issues.description: revoke_error may leak sensitive backend details to lease lookup callers
issues.detail: RevokeErr originates from backend revocation failures and can contain connection strings, internal hostnames, credentials, or stack traces. Exposing it via the lease lookup API broadens its audience beyond operators reading server logs. The PR author flagged this concern explicitly. Consider gating behind a sudo capability or redacting to a generic 'revocation failed' indicator while keeping details in logs.

issues.description: Exported FetchLeaseTimes renamed without alias, breaking external consumers
issues.detail: FetchLeaseTimes is an exported method on ExpirationManager. Renaming it to FetchLeaseInfo with no shim breaks any downstream code or plugin importing vault as a library. At minimum keep a thin FetchLeaseTimes wrapper that delegates to FetchLeaseInfo (or document the break in the changelog as a breaking change rather than 'improvement').

issues.description: OpenAPI marks 'path' as Required but lookup of pre-existing leases may have empty Path
issues.detail: The new response field 'path' is declared Required: true in logical_system_paths.go, yet leaseEntry.Path on older persisted leases could be empty and is always emitted regardless of value. If any code path produces a lease with empty Path, schema-validating clients will reject the response. Either drop Required, or guarantee the field is always populated.

issues.description: Mixing nil and t.Context() in the same test is inconsistent
issues.detail: TestExpiration_revokeEntry_rejected_fairsharing was changed to use namespace.RootContext(t.Context()) for the renamed call but other RootContext(nil) calls in the same test remain. Either keep nil for consistency with surrounding code, or update all sites. The mixed style invites confusion about why this one call needs a real context.

issues.description: namespace_path omitted when namespace is root rather than returned as empty string
issues.detail: The handler only sets namespace_path when leaseInfo.namespace != nil and Path != "". For root-namespace leases the key is absent entirely, while OpenAPI declares it as a string field. Clients reading the response will see inconsistent shapes; consider always emitting "" for the root namespace so the schema matches reality.

issues.description: Test coverage missing for the new namespace_path and revoke_error fields
issues.detail: logical_system_test.go only asserts the new 'path' field. The two other new response fields (namespace_path, revoke_error) have no test coverage, so regressions in the namespace/RevokeErr propagation through leaseInfoForExport would go undetected. Add at least one assertion each — for namespace_path with a non-root NS and revoke_error after a forced revocation failure.

review.summary: The PR cleanly renames FetchLeaseTimes → FetchLeaseInfo and threads three new fields (path, namespace_path, revoke_error) through to the lease lookup response, with matching docs and a changelog entry. The main risks are the security/exposure question the author already raised about revoke_error (which can carry backend-leaked details), a silent break of an exported API surface, and an OpenAPI schema that marks 'path' Required while the handler can in principle emit empty/missing values. Test coverage only exercises the new 'path' field — namespace_path and revoke_error paths are untested. Nothing here is blocking-correctness, but the revoke_error exposure deserves a decision before merge.
